definition: P31 constituency-level evidence-state closures for the four TSC/NEMIS-derived education establishment indicators (IND-PUBLIC-PRIMARY-SCHOOLS, IND-PRIMARY-CLASSROOM-TEACHERS, IND-PUBLIC-SECONDARY-SCHOOLS, IND-SECONDARY-TEACHERS). These four indicators are outside the P18 public-taxonomy slot set (data/indicators/seed/placeholder-taxonomy.json carries no county, constituency or ward slot for them at all -- they surface only through the raw canonical indicator registry and the P26-P30 local-54 framework), so a genuinely researched, specifically-cited constituency closure for them cannot live in the shared data/completeness/evidence-states.json without breaking that file's P18-specific, exact-count reconciliation (scripts/completeness/validate-slot-ledger.mjs). This file is consumed only by scripts/p29/build-local-54-slot-ledger.mjs, exactly like data/completeness/evidence-states.json, but scoped to indicators/levels the older P18 taxonomy never covered. It never manufactures a zero, proxy, regional inheritance or synthetic observation.

states.period_label: TSC 2023 establishment, county-only tabulation (Appendix 4.5, PWPER July 2023 report) -- no constituency-level publication exists
states.source: Teachers Service Commission (TSC) 2023 establishment data, as tabulated by county in the Ministry of Education's Presidential Working Party on Education Reform (PWPER) report
states.reason: P31 conducted a genuine, multi-source investigation into constituency-level administrative data for Kenya's TSC/NEMIS-derived education establishment indicators before closing this cell, rather than assuming unavailability or spatially allocating the county figure. Findings, each independently checked: (1) NEMIS (nemis.education.go.ke) -- the Ministry of Education's National Education Management Information System, the underlying institution-level registry that both TSC and the Ministry draw on -- is not usable as an open data source: its HTTPS endpoint fails TLS handshake outright (curl error 35, schannel), and the plain-HTTP fallback (confirmed reachable, HTTP 200) serves only a username/password ASP.NET login screen for school/institution enrolment, with no public school-locator, constituency-filter search or bulk export; access requires credentials issued to County/Sub-County Directors of Education. This mirrors this project's prior, independent finding that KMHFR is nominally open but unreachable in practice. (2) opendata.go.ke, the national open-data portal (an ArcGIS Hub deployment), could not be used for dataset discovery: its dataset-search API returned HTTP 401 'Subscription is canceled, the item is not accessible' when queried directly, and no NEMIS/school dataset could be located through it. (3) The Ministry of Education's own periodic 'Basic Education Statistical Booklet' (2020 edition downloaded and its full text inspected; 2014/2016/2019 editions independently confirmed to exist with the same structure) tabulates school counts and teacher counts only down to county level -- its own table of contents lists Annexes I-III as 'Tables by County', and no sub-county, constituency or ward table appears in any edition located. (4) KNBS's Economic Survey (2024 edition's Chapter 15 'Education and Training' tables workbook downloaded and inspected sheet by sheet; the 2026 edition was also confirmed to exist) publishes these same series as national time series only, with zero geographic breakdown below the national total for schools or teachers -- the only geographically disaggregated Chapter 15 table (15.27, adult-education enrolment) covers an unrelated indicator. (5) TSC's own website (tsc.go.ke) publishes no staffing-establishment or teacher-deployment dataset broken down by sub-county or constituency; the only 'Staffing Norms' publication found in its downloads catalogue is a procurement consultancy advert, not a data release. (6) KNBS's 2024 National School Census -- the one current national effort that would, if published, produce genuine institution-level (and therefore constituency/ward-taggable) records, since its own field questionnaire explicitly captures Constituency and Ward for every institution enumerated (fields EA06/EA07 etc. on the identification panel) -- has to date published only a Pilot Report (dated January 2025; downloaded and inspected directly) covering 8 of Kenya's 47 selected counties and 674 institutions, conducted to test instruments and logistics. The main nationwide census, whose field data collection concluded around July 2024 per contemporaneous Ministry/KNBS reporting, has not had a results report, aggregate tables or microdata release published as of this review (2026-09-18) -- over two years after fieldwork concluded. (7) The county-level public primary school count figure this Atlas already carries for this indicator traces to Appendix 4.5 ("Current Teacher Establishment in Public Primary Schools, 2023 Showing Shortages by County") of the Ministry of Education's July 2023 Presidential Working Party on Education Reform (PWPER) report, sourced there as 'TSC 2023'; that appendix itself presents only 47 county-level rows, with no underlying institution-level extract attached, linked or referenced anywhere in the report. No official constituency-level or ward-level publication of this indicator exists, and no defensible, disclosed crosswalk from any lower administrative tier to the 290 IEBC-delimited constituencies could be constructed, because no lower-tier (sub-county, zone or institution-level) tabulation of this indicator was found published anywhere. Per this project's anti-fabrication rule, the county TSC 2023 figure is never spatially allocated down into the 290 constituency rows; this cell is closed as official_unavailable pending a genuine constituency-level source (most plausibly the still-unpublished main 2024 National School Census).
states.refresh_trigger: KNBS publishes the main 2024 National School Census results (which, per its own field questionnaire, capture Constituency and Ward per institution), or NEMIS/TSC publish a public, credential-free institution-level export or constituency-filtered locator that can be aggregated with a disclosed crosswalk to the Atlas's 290 current-boundary constituencies, or the Ministry of Education's Basic Education Statistical Booklet begins publishing a sub-county/constituency annex.
